nodes.name: scipy_remediation_root
nodes.description: Source-aligned SciPy remediation atoms for sparse graph routines and normal distribution freezing.

nodes.name: graph_laplacian
nodes.description: Return SciPy's graph Laplacian matrix for a square weighted adjacency matrix.
nodes.type_signature: (W: SparseGraphInput, normed: bool = False, use_out_degree: bool = False, symmetrized: bool = False) -> SparseGraphOutput
nodes.complexity_reasoning: SciPy's sparse graph Laplacian scales linearly with the number of nodes N and edges E, taking O(N + E) time and space.

nodes.name: single_source_shortest_path
nodes.description: Return shortest-path distances from one or more selected SciPy graph source nodes.
nodes.type_signature: (csgraph: SparseGraphInput, indices: np.ndarray | int = 0, method: str = 'auto', directed: bool = True, return_predecessors: bool = False, unweighted: bool = False, overwrite: bool = False) -> tuple[np.ndarray, ...] | np.ndarray
nodes.complexity_reasoning: Computing shortest paths from S sources using Dijkstra's algorithm on a graph of size N and E edges takes O(S * (E + N log N)) time and O(S * N) space.

nodes.name: all_pairs_shortest_path
nodes.description: Return all-pairs shortest-path distances with SciPy's sparse graph shortest-path API.
nodes.type_signature: (csgraph: SparseGraphInput, method: str = 'auto', directed: bool = True, return_predecessors: bool = False, unweighted: bool = False, overwrite: bool = False) -> tuple[np.ndarray, ...] | np.ndarray
nodes.complexity_reasoning: All-pairs shortest paths using Dijkstra's algorithm for each of the N source nodes takes O(N * (E + N log N)) time and O(N^2) space.

nodes.name: minimum_spanning_tree
nodes.description: Return SciPy's sparse minimum spanning tree for a weighted graph.
nodes.complexity_reasoning: Finding the minimum spanning tree of a graph with N nodes and E edges using Prim's or Kruskal's algorithm takes O(E log N) time and O(N + E) space.

nodes.name: graph_fourier_transform
nodes.description: Project a graph signal onto a Laplacian eigenbasis.
nodes.type_signature: (L: SparseGraphInput, x: NDArray[np.float64], k: int | None = None) -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.float64]]
nodes.complexity_reasoning: Computing the eigendecomposition of the N x N graph Laplacian takes O(N^3) time and O(N^2) space for full bases, or O(k * (E + N)) for k sparse eigenspace steps.

nodes.name: inverse_graph_fourier_transform
nodes.description: Reconstruct a graph signal from graph Fourier coefficients and a supplied eigenbasis.
nodes.complexity_reasoning: Reconstructing the graph signal is a matrix-vector product of an N x k eigenbasis and a k-dimensional coefficient vector, taking O(k * N) time and O(N) space.

nodes.name: heat_kernel_diffusion
nodes.description: Smooth a graph signal by applying exp(-tL) in the Laplacian spectral basis.
nodes.type_signature: (L: SparseGraphInput, x: NDArray[np.float64], t: float, k: int | None = None) -> NDArray[np.float64]
nodes.complexity_reasoning: Smoothing via spectral heat diffusion requires computing the Laplacian eigenbasis, taking O(N^3) time and O(N^2) space in the full case.

nodes.name: norm
nodes.description: Freeze SciPy's normal distribution for a finite location and positive scale.
nodes.complexity_reasoning: Freezing a normal distribution creates a lightweight configuration object in constant O(1) time and space.

nodes.name: idct
nodes.description: Inverse Discrete Cosine Transform. Reconstruct spatial-domain signal from DCT frequency coefficients.
nodes.type_signature: (x: NDArray, type: int, n: int | None, axis: int, norm: str | None) -> NDArray
nodes.complexity_reasoning: The Inverse Discrete Cosine Transform along an axis of length N is computed using the Fast Fourier Transform in O(N log N) time and O(N) space.

metadata.scope_note: The sparse_graph family contains direct scipy.sparse.csgraph wrappers and SciPy-backed graph signal processing helpers. Graph Fourier and heat-kernel rows are not direct csgraph parity APIs.
